what.text: A 'Bestseller' section that shows a row or grid of top-selling product cards. From the review feedback, each card has a product image, a short teaser text, a star rating, a price and a discount indicator. The ticket is a design review of the launched section, not a spec, so this composition is inferred from the feedback.

why.text: Labelling products as bestsellers is social proof: shoppers assume that what many others bought is a safe, good choice. Star ratings add to this and lower perceived risk. Showing the discount next to the price anchors value and makes the deal obvious. Putting proven products up front shortens the path to a first product for new visitors.

how.text: Add a product-grid section (collection-driven, e.g. a 'Bestsellers' collection or best-selling sort) with cards. Each card shows: the product image, a star rating (review app), a title, a one-line unique teaser (e.g. from a metafield), the current price, the compare-at price and a discount badge. Reviewer guidance: make the discount badge more prominent relative to the price, keep teaser texts distinct per product, and make sure every product has a real price (one product showed €0.00) and an image.

items: Desktop vs. mobile layout (grid vs. swipe row)

dependencies.text: A bestseller collection, product images, compare-at prices for discount calculation, and a reviews app for star ratings (not live at launch). A per-product teaser text field (probably a metafield) is likely. The page placement is not stated in the ticket; Home is an assumption.

items: Revenue per session for sessions that saw the section
Share of orders containing bestseller products
